query: Why do resolution duration values vary across tickets?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: The numeric resolution duration itself -- the outcome whose variation is being explained.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: Priority is a candidate cause of resolution duration; a plausible treatment whose effect is being attributed.

per_column.name: is_network
per_column.rationale: Category indicator; candidate cause of duration. One-hot slice of the category variable, a candidate driver rather than a common cause.

per_column.name: is_database
per_column.rationale: Category indicator serving as another candidate driver of duration.

per_column.name: is_software
per_column.rationale: Category indicator; candidate driver of duration.

per_column.name: is_hardware
per_column.rationale: Category indicator; candidate driver of duration.

per_column.name: duration_category
per_column.rationale: A binned version of the outcome itself, not an explanatory variable.

per_column.name: priority_avg_duration
per_column.rationale: Group-mean of the outcome by priority -- a target-derived aggregate, essentially leakage from the outcome, not a confounder.

per_column.name: category_avg_duration
per_column.rationale: Group-mean of the outcome by category -- outcome-derived aggregate, not a common cause.

per_column.name: duration_vs_priority_avg
per_column.rationale: Deviation of the outcome from its own group mean -- a transformation of the outcome, not a predictor/confounder.

per_column.name: duration_vs_category_avg
per_column.rationale: Outcome deviation from category mean -- derived from the outcome, not a confounder.

per_column.name: assignee_avg_duration
per_column.rationale: Assignee historical average duration could proxy an assignee/skill effect that plausibly influences both assignment (which tickets/priorities go to whom) and duration; however it is largely outcome-derived, weakening its status.

per_column.name: duration_vs_assignee_avg
per_column.rationale: Outcome deviation from assignee mean -- derived from the outcome, not a confounder.

per_column.name: has_round_duration
per_column.rationale: Degenerate flag (all zeros); noise, no causal role.

judge.rationale: The set supplies candidate treatments (priority, category one-hots) but essentially NO genuine confounders. A confounder must be a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome that is not derived from the outcome. Almost all remaining columns are outcome-derived aggregates or deviations (priority_avg_duration, category_avg_duration, assignee_avg_duration, and the *_vs_*_avg deviations) -- these are transformations of the outcome itself, constituting target leakage rather than confounding adjustment. There are no independent covariates such as ticket complexity, workload/queue length at open time, reassignment count, business hours, caller/requester attributes, or assignment-group capacity that would plausibly cause both which priority/category a ticket gets and how long it takes. Because the system surfaced no true common-cause covariates and instead recycled the outcome into group means, the causal-attribution capability under test is not realised.
